stem: A 4-month-old infant has a first typical UTI that responded to antibiotics and grew Escherichia coli; what imaging follow-up is appropriate?

options.text: Immediate ultrasound in the emergency department
No imaging unless the infection recurs
Mandatory MCUG and DMSA scan regardless of ultrasound result
Repeat urine culture in 6 weeks instead of imaging

explanation: A non-acute ultrasound within 6 weeks is the appropriate follow-up for this infant with a first typical UTI. This is because infants under 6 months with a first typical UTI should have renal tract ultrasound arranged electively within 6 weeks to look for urinary tract anomalies.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this is not usually required urgently for a typical UTI that is responding to treatment.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because infants under 6 months still need imaging follow-up after a first typical UTI.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because infants under 6 months with a first typical UTI should have renal tract ultrasound arranged electively within 6 weeks to look for urinary tract anomalies.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because MCUG and DMSA are not routinely mandatory for every infant and depend on the clinical course and ultrasound findings.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because repeat culture does not replace the recommended imaging follow-up in this age group.

source.hint: Determine the age cutoff and whether the imaging needs to be performed urgently or electively.
